description: Development observations, not a success-rate benchmark. Images and full responses remain in ignored local artifacts; hashes are SHA256 of the exact data URL string. Initial and follow-up episodes used different prompt/UI versions. Rubik reset uses a random one-turn scramble. Historical UI status messages have been translated to English; model choices, probabilities and image hashes are unchanged.

action.instructions: You control a real 2x2 Rubik's cube. The screenshot is a six-face unfolded net: U above F; L, F, R, B across the middle; D below F. Each sticker contains its color initial (W white, Y yellow, O orange, R red, G green, B blue). Face names identify positions, not current sticker colors. Goal: make all four stickers on EACH of the six faces the same color. Select the single face turn most likely to restore all six solid-color faces. Moves without a prime turn 90 degrees clockwise when viewing that face directly from outside. Prime moves turn counterclockwise. Each action rotates a full cube layer, including adjacent stickers. Infer the move only from the screenshot; no hidden state or scramble history is supplied.
